ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the non-inverting input terminal marked “+” at the lower end of the operational amplifier is connected to node n, and node n is connected through a 2 kΩ resistor to a 1 V power supply; the inverting input terminal marked “−” at the upper end is connected to node m, and node m is grounded through a 3 kΩ resistor; the output terminal is marked U0, and there is a 6 kΩ resistor connected back from the output terminal to the connectable point P at the upper left, with P located above node m. Then reason: if P is connected to m, then the 6 kΩ resistor becomes the feedback resistor from the output terminal to the inverting input terminal, and the 3 kΩ resistor becomes the voltage-dividing resistor from the inverting terminal to ground. The input current of an ideal operational amplifier is approximately zero, so there is no voltage drop across the 2 kΩ, V+ = 1 V. Under negative feedback, V− = V+ = 1 V, therefore this circuit is a non-inverting amplifier, and the output U0 = (1 + 6 kΩ/3 kΩ) × 1 V = 3 V. The problem requires U0 = 3 V, so P must be connected to point m.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: identify the lower '+' input node n fed by 1 V through 2 kΩ, the upper '−' input node m tied to ground through 3 kΩ, and the 6 kΩ resistor from output U0 to the switch point P. If P is connected to m, the 6 kΩ resistor forms the feedback resistor from output to the inverting input, while the 3 kΩ resistor is the lower divider resistor to ground. Since the ideal op-amp input draws no current, V+ = 1 V. Under negative feedback V− = V+ = 1 V, so U0 = (1 + 6 kΩ/3 kΩ)·1 V = 3 V. Therefore P must be connected to m.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram and list the candidate connection points for P. Test P connected to n: then the output is fed back to the '+' input, while the '−' input m is only tied to ground through 3 kΩ, so V− = 0 V. This is positive feedback/no negative feedback and cannot produce a stable linear U0 = 3 V with V+ equal to V−. Test P connected to m: then the output is fed back through 6 kΩ to the '−' input, and m also has 3 kΩ to ground, giving negative feedback. The '+' input n is at 1 V because no current flows through the 2 kΩ resistor. The feedback divider gives Vm = U0·3/(6+3). Setting Vm = Vn = 1 V gives U0 = 3 V. Hence the only consistent connection is P to m.
